water: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry; less in winter. Never leave it standing in water.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; tolerates low light but grows slower. Direct midday sun scorches the leaves.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer (e.g. NPK 10-10-10) at half strength, spring to summer; none in winter.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Usually overwatering: let the soil dry more between waterings.

problems.title: Brown, crispy leaf edges
problems.hint: Dry air or underwatering.

problems.title: Mealybugs
problems.hint: White cottony spots: wipe off with cotton and rubbing alcohol, repeat weekly.

water: Water when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry; reduce in winter.
sunHint: Bright indirect light gives bigger, more split leaves; avoid harsh direct sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in spring and summer.

problems.title: Leaves without splits
problems.hint: Too little light, or a young plant: move it to brighter indirect light.

problems.title: Yellow lower leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering or poor drainage; check the pot has holes.

problems.title: Brown spots with yellow halo
problems.hint: Often fungal from wet leaves or soil: water the soil, not the leaves, and improve airflow.

water: Let the soil dry out completely between waterings; every 3-4 weeks in winter.
sunHint: Very adaptable: from low light to some direct sun. Grows best in bright light.
fertilizer: Cactus/succulent fertilizer or diluted balanced fertilizer, only in the warm months.

problems.title: Soft, mushy base
problems.hint: Root rot from overwatering: remove rotten parts, repot in dry, fast-draining soil.

problems.title: Leaves falling over
problems.hint: Too much water or too little light.

problems.title: Wrinkled leaves
problems.hint: Thirsty: water thoroughly once.

water: Water only when the soil is completely dry; its thick rhizomes store water.
sunHint: Tolerates low light well; bright indirect light makes it grow faster. Avoid direct sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength, 2-3 times in spring and summer.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Almost always overwatering: let it dry out and water less often.

problems.title: Stems collapsing
problems.hint: Rotting rhizome from wet soil: check roots, repot in fast-draining mix.

water: Keep the soil lightly moist; it droops when thirsty and recovers quickly after watering.
sunHint: Medium to low indirect light; more light means more flowers. No direct sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in spring and summer.

problems.title: Drooping plant
problems.hint: Thirsty: water well. If the soil is wet, check for root rot.

problems.title: Brown leaf tips
problems.hint: Dry air, too much fertilizer, or chlorine/fluoride in tap water.

problems.title: No flowers
problems.hint: Too little light: move it to brighter indirect light.

water: Keep the soil constantly moist, never soggy. Ferns dislike drying out. (Care varies among fern species.)
sunHint: Bright indirect light or light shade; direct sun burns the fronds.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at quarter to half strength in the growing season.

problems.title: Fronds turning brown and dry
problems.hint: Low humidity or soil drying out: water more regularly, mist or group plants.

problems.title: Leaflets dropping
problems.hint: Dry air, drafts or too little light.

water: Water when the top 2-3 cm are dry; likes humidity but not soggy roots.
sunHint: Bright indirect light for flowering; direct sun burns the leaves.
fertilizer: Fertilizer richer in phosphorus (e.g. NPK 10-30-10) at half strength to encourage flowers.

problems.title: No new flowers
problems.hint: Too little light or not enough nutrients.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering or old leaves aging naturally.

problems.title: Brown leaf tips
problems.hint: Low humidity or salt build-up: flush the soil with water now and then.

water: Water when the top few cm are dry; less in winter.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; tolerates shade. Avoid direct sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in spring and summer.

problems.title: Lower leaves yellowing
problems.hint: Normal aging, or overwatering if many at once.

problems.title: Leggy stem
problems.hint: Too little light; the top can be cut and rooted.

problems.title: Irritating sap
problems.hint: The sap irritates mouth and skin: wear gloves when pruning.

water: Keep the soil lightly moist; use rain or filtered water if tap water browns the tips.
sunHint: Medium indirect light; direct sun fades and burns the leaves.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in the growing season.

problems.title: Crispy brown edges
problems.hint: Low humidity or hard tap water.

problems.title: Curled leaves
problems.hint: Underwatering or dry air.

problems.title: Spider mites
problems.hint: Fine webbing under leaves: shower the plant, raise humidity, repeat.

water: Keep the soil evenly moist, never soggy; prefers filtered or rain water. (Care varies among species.)
sunHint: Medium indirect light; no direct sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in spring and summer.

problems.title: Brown, crispy edges
problems.hint: Low humidity or minerals in tap water.

problems.title: Leaves curling
problems.hint: Thirsty or air too dry.

problems.title: Spider mites
problems.hint: Check leaf undersides; wash leaves and increase humidity.

water: Water when the top half of the soil is dry.
sunHint: Medium to bright indirect light; tolerates lower light.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength, spring to summer.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering: let the soil dry more.

problems.title: Small leaves, long gaps on stems
problems.hint: Not enough light.

water: Water when the top few cm are dry; its thick petioles store some water.
sunHint: Bright indirect light or light shade; morning sun is fine.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in the warm months.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering or poor drainage.

problems.title: Burnt patches
problems.hint: Too much direct afternoon sun.

water: Keep the soil lightly moist, letting the top dry slightly between waterings.
sunHint: Bright indirect light keeps the colours; no harsh sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in the growing season.

problems.title: Leggy growth
problems.hint: Too little light; pinch back to keep it bushy.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering.

water: Semi-succulent: let the soil dry well between waterings.
sunHint: Medium to bright indirect light.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength, a few times in spring and summer.

problems.title: Wilting with wet soil
problems.hint: Root rot from overwatering: let it dry, repot if needed.

problems.title: Leaves dropping
problems.hint: Cold drafts or sudden changes.

water: Water when the top half of the soil is dry.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; rotate the pot weekly so it grows straight.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in spring and summer.

problems.title: Leaves curling down (doming)
problems.hint: Too much light or too little water.

problems.title: Leaning plant
problems.hint: Growing towards the light: turn the pot regularly.

water: Water when the top few cm are dry; its fleshy roots store water.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; tolerates some morning sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in the growing season.

problems.title: Brown leaf tips
problems.hint: Fluoride/chlorine in tap water or dry air; trim the tips.

problems.title: No baby plants
problems.hint: Too little light or pot too large.

water: Water when the top half of the soil is dry.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; tolerates lower light.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength, spring to summer.

problems.title: Brown leaf tips
problems.hint: Sensitive to fluoride in tap water and dry air.

problems.title: Yellow lower leaves
problems.hint: Normal shedding, or overwatering if many.

water: Water thoroughly when the top 5 cm are dry; keep a steady routine.
sunHint: Lots of bright light, some gentle direct sun; dislikes being moved.
fertilizer: Balanced or nitrogen-rich liquid fertilizer (e.g. NPK 3-1-2) in spring and summer.

problems.title: Brown spots on leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering (spots from the centre) or underwatering (from the edges).

problems.title: Leaves dropping
problems.hint: Moved, drafts or sudden light change: keep it in one spot.

water: Water when the top few cm are dry; less in winter.
sunHint: Bright light with some direct morning sun.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in the growing season.

problems.title: Lower leaves dropping
problems.hint: Overwatering or too little light.

problems.title: Dusty leaves
problems.hint: Wipe with a damp cloth so they can photosynthesize.

water: Keep the soil lightly moist in summer; let the top dry a little in winter.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; outdoors, partial shade.
fertilizer: Palm fertilizer or balanced fertilizer with micronutrients (magnesium, iron) in spring and summer.

problems.title: Brown frond tips
problems.hint: Dry air, salt build-up or irregular watering.

problems.title: Yellowing fronds
problems.hint: Nutrient deficiency (often magnesium) or overwatering.

water: Water when the top few cm are dry.
sunHint: Medium to low indirect light; direct sun yellows the leaves.
fertilizer: Palm or balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in the warm months.

problems.title: Brown tips
problems.hint: Dry air or salts in the soil: flush with water occasionally.

problems.title: Scale insects
problems.hint: Small brown bumps on stems: scrape off, treat with neem oil.

water: Water when the top 2 cm are dry; avoid wetting the leaves. (Care varies among begonias.)
sunHint: Bright indirect light; some morning sun for flowering types.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength; bloom fertilizer for flowering types.

problems.title: Powdery mildew
problems.hint: White powder on leaves: improve airflow, avoid wet leaves, remove affected leaves.

problems.title: Stem rot
problems.hint: Overwatering: let the soil dry more.

water: Water from below or at the soil with room-temperature water; keep leaves dry.
sunHint: Bright indirect light, e.g. near an east window.
fertilizer: African violet fertilizer (higher phosphorus) at low strength.

problems.title: Spots on leaves
problems.hint: Cold water on the leaves: water the soil only.

problems.title: No flowers
problems.hint: Not enough light or fertilizer.

problems.title: Crown rot
problems.hint: Soggy soil: let it dry slightly, use a light mix.

water: Water when the roots turn silvery (about weekly); drain completely. Grow in bark, not soil. (Other orchids differ.)
sunHint: Bright indirect light; no midday sun.
fertilizer: Orchid fertilizer at quarter to half strength ('weakly, weekly' style).

problems.title: Wrinkled, limp leaves
problems.hint: Root problems: check for rotten (brown, mushy) roots.

problems.title: No new flower spike
problems.hint: A slight night-time temperature drop in autumn helps it rebloom.

problems.title: Crown rot
problems.hint: Water left in the leaf base: water in the morning and tilt to drain.

water: Keep a little water in the central cup (refresh it weekly) and keep the mix barely moist.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; no strong direct sun.
fertilizer: Very diluted liquid fertilizer, rarely; bromeliads need little feeding.

problems.title: Mother plant dying after flowering
problems.hint: Normal: it produces pups; grow those on.

problems.title: Rotting base
problems.hint: Soil too wet: water the cup, not the soil.

water: Keep the soil lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; tolerates shade. Prefers cooler spots.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength in the growing season.

problems.title: Spider mites
problems.hint: Common in warm, dry air: shower the leaves regularly.

problems.title: Crispy leaves
problems.hint: Too hot or too dry.

water: Water deeply only when the soil is completely dry; much less in winter.
sunHint: Full sun to bright light; a sunny window or outdoors.
fertilizer: Cactus/succulent fertilizer at half strength, a couple of times in the warm season.

problems.title: Soft, translucent leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering: stop watering until dry.

problems.title: Thin, curling leaves
problems.hint: Thirsty, or too little light.

problems.title: Brown/red leaves
problems.hint: Sun stress after a sudden move to strong sun: acclimate gradually.

water: Let the soil dry completely; water less in winter.
sunHint: Several hours of sun; red leaf edges are normal in strong light.
fertilizer: Succulent fertilizer at half strength in spring and summer.

problems.title: Shriveled leaves
problems.hint: Underwatering: water deeply.

problems.title: Leaves dropping
problems.hint: Overwatering or sudden cold.

problems.title: Mealybugs
problems.hint: White fluff in leaf joints: dab with alcohol.

water: Soak and dry: water thoroughly, then wait until the soil is fully dry. Keep water off the rosette.
sunHint: Lots of direct sun; indoors, the sunniest window.
fertilizer: Succulent fertilizer at low strength in the growing season.

problems.title: Stretched, pale growth
problems.hint: Etiolation from too little light: move to more sun.

problems.title: Mushy leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering or water in the rosette.

water: Let the soil dry between waterings; it's a succulent.
sunHint: Bright light with some direct sun for flowering.
fertilizer: Bloom fertilizer (higher phosphorus) at half strength during growth.

problems.title: Not reblooming
problems.hint: Needs short days: about 6 weeks of 14 hours of darkness each night.

problems.title: Rotting stems
problems.hint: Overwatering.

water: Water deeply only when the soil is bone dry; almost none in winter. (Forest cacti like Christmas cactus need more.)
sunHint: As much direct sun as possible.
fertilizer: Cactus fertilizer (low nitrogen) at half strength in the warm season.

problems.title: Soft, dark base
problems.hint: Rot from overwatering: usually fatal, cut and re-root healthy parts.

problems.title: Leaning or thin growth
problems.hint: Not enough sun.

water: Keep the soil moist but not soggy; water at the base in the morning.
sunHint: At least 6 hours of sun.
fertilizer: Balanced or nitrogen-rich organic fertilizer (e.g. worm castings) monthly.

problems.title: Flowering and fewer leaves
problems.hint: Pinch off flower buds and harvest tips often to keep it bushy.

problems.title: Black spots / wilting
problems.hint: Fungal disease from wet leaves or cold: water the soil, give airflow.

problems.title: Aphids
problems.hint: Small insects on tips: hose off or use soapy water.

water: Let the soil dry between waterings; it hates soggy roots.
sunHint: Full sun, at least 6 hours.
fertilizer: Light feeding only: a little organic fertilizer in spring.

problems.title: Needles browning from the base
problems.hint: Root rot from overwatering or poor drainage.

problems.title: Powdery mildew
problems.hint: Too humid and shaded: more sun and airflow.

water: Keep the soil consistently moist.
sunHint: Sun to part shade; afternoon shade helps in hot weather.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer monthly in the growing season.

problems.title: Spreads aggressively
problems.hint: Grow it in its own pot.

problems.title: Rust (orange spots)
problems.hint: Remove affected leaves, avoid wetting foliage.

water: Keep the soil lightly moist.
sunHint: Full sun to part shade.
fertilizer: Nitrogen-rich organic fertilizer after harvests.

problems.title: Yellow tips
problems.hint: Irregular watering or lack of nitrogen.

problems.title: Thrips
problems.hint: Silvery streaks on leaves: rinse, use soapy water.

water: Keep the soil evenly moist.
sunHint: Sun to part shade.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer monthly.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering or too little nitrogen.

problems.title: Bolting (flowering)
problems.hint: Heat or age: it's a biennial, resow periodically.

water: Keep the soil moist; it bolts when stressed.
sunHint: Sun in mild weather, afternoon shade in hot weather.
fertilizer: Light organic fertilizer; too much nitrogen reduces flavour.

problems.title: Quickly goes to seed
problems.hint: Heat and dry soil: sow small batches every few weeks.

water: Let the soil dry between waterings.
sunHint: Full sun for the best flavour.
fertilizer: Little feeding needed: light organic fertilizer in spring.

problems.title: Root rot
problems.hint: Overwatering or heavy soil: use a well-draining mix.

water: Let the soil dry between waterings; drought tolerant.
sunHint: Full sun.
fertilizer: Very little: a light organic feed in spring.

problems.title: Woody, sparse plant
problems.hint: Trim lightly after flowering to keep it compact.

problems.title: Rotting
problems.hint: Too much water.

water: Keep the soil evenly moist; mulch helps in heat.
sunHint: Full sun, 6-8 hours.
fertilizer: Balanced fertilizer while growing, then one richer in potassium (e.g. NPK 4-14-8) when flowering and fruiting.

problems.title: Flowers dropping
problems.hint: Heat stress or irregular watering.

problems.title: Aphids and whiteflies
problems.hint: Check leaf undersides; soapy water or neem oil.

water: Let the soil dry out between waterings; very sensitive to wet roots.
sunHint: Full sun, at least 6-8 hours.
fertilizer: Little or no feeding; poor, well-drained soil suits it.

problems.title: Grey, dying stems
problems.hint: Root rot from humidity and wet soil: improve drainage.

problems.title: Few flowers
problems.hint: Not enough sun or too much fertilizer.

water: Water deeply at the base, keeping leaves dry.
sunHint: At least 6 hours of sun.
fertilizer: Rose or flowering-plant fertilizer (e.g. NPK 4-14-8) during the growing season.

problems.title: Black spot
problems.hint: Fungal spots on leaves: remove them, water the soil only, improve airflow.

problems.title: Aphids
problems.hint: On buds: hose off or soapy water.

problems.title: Powdery mildew
problems.hint: White powder: more sun and airflow.

water: Keep the soil moist in heat and flowering; less in winter.
sunHint: Full sun for abundant flowers.
fertilizer: Fertilizer richer in potassium, lower in phosphorus, during flowering.

problems.title: Buds dropping
problems.hint: Irregular watering, heat stress or moving the plant.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Over/underwatering or nutrient deficiency.

problems.title: Whiteflies and aphids
problems.hint: Treat with soapy water or neem oil.

water: Water when dry; slightly dry conditions encourage flowering.
sunHint: Full sun; the more sun, the more colour.
fertilizer: Low-nitrogen, higher-potassium fertilizer; too much nitrogen gives leaves instead of flowers.

problems.title: No flowers
problems.hint: Too little sun, too much water or too much nitrogen.

problems.title: Leaves dropping
problems.hint: Sudden change or overwatering; usually recovers.

water: Water when the top few cm are dry; avoid soggy soil.
sunHint: Full sun to bright light.
fertilizer: Balanced or bloom fertilizer at half strength during flowering.

problems.title: Yellow leaves
problems.hint: Overwatering.

problems.title: Grey mould on flowers
problems.hint: Remove spent flowers, improve airflow.

water: Water when the top few cm are dry; drought tolerant once established. Much less in cool weather, when it may drop leaves.
sunHint: Full sun, at least 6 hours, for abundant flowers; tolerates light shade but flowers less.
fertilizer: Bloom fertilizer richer in phosphorus (e.g. NPK 10-30-10 or 4-14-8) in the warm season; none in winter.

problems.title: Few or no flowers
problems.hint: Not enough sun, or too much nitrogen: move to full sun and use a bloom fertilizer.

problems.title: Leaves dropping in winter
problems.hint: Normal in cooler months; reduce watering until new growth appears.

problems.title: Rust (orange powder under leaves)
problems.hint: Remove affected leaves and fallen debris; improve airflow.

problems.title: Mealybugs and whiteflies
problems.hint: Check leaf undersides; wipe off or treat with neem oil or soapy water.

water: Water when the soil is dry a few cm down; drought tolerant in the ground, pots need more frequent watering.
sunHint: Full sun; in shade it flowers poorly and gets powdery mildew.
fertilizer: Light feeding with a balanced or bloom fertilizer in the growing season; too much fertilizer gives leaves instead of flowers.

problems.title: Powdery mildew
problems.hint: White powder on leaves: more sun and airflow, water at the base.

problems.title: Whiteflies and lace bugs
problems.hint: Pale speckled leaves: rinse undersides, use soapy water or neem oil.

problems.title: Spreads by seed
problems.hint: Its berries spread easily (it's invasive in many regions): remove spent flower heads. The berries are poisonous.

water: In water: keep the roots covered and change the water every 1-2 weeks, using filtered or rain water. In soil: keep it lightly moist.
sunHint: Bright indirect light; tolerates low light. Direct sun yellows and scorches the leaves.
fertilizer: A drop of very diluted liquid fertilizer (made for lucky bamboo or houseplants) every 1-2 months; too much burns it.

problems.title: Yellow leaves or stalks
problems.hint: Too much sun, too much fertilizer, or chlorine/fluoride in tap water: use filtered water.

problems.title: Green algae in the water
problems.hint: Light reaching the water: use an opaque container and change the water more often.

problems.title: Soft, rotting stalk
problems.hint: Remove it so the rot doesn't spread; refresh the water and rinse the container.
